DATA_DIR: Folder holding .mtf/.board inputs (2026-10-18). Relative paths below resolve against this.
MANUAL_ROLLS: debugging aid - prompts for each roll instead of
USE_TMM: rolling randomly. Only sane with NUM_SIMULATIONS=1.
NUM_SIMULATIONS: to the to-hit threshold before rolling. NOTE 2026-10-18: not read by the integration path - TMM always comes from actual hexes moved (combat.fc_to_tmm), per Daniel 2026-10-18.
MAX_TURNS: hard cap on turns per simulated battle.
SEED: BattleRNG seed for a reproducible batch. None = fresh entropy.
WORKERS: Each battle gets its own seed made from this one (orchestrator.battle_seed): battle 1 uses SEED itself. Parallel batches (2026-10-20): how many battles run at once, one per CPU core. 0 = one worker per core; 1 = one battle after another (no extra processes). The output is identical either way - each battle has its own seed, and the parent prints every battle's log in order. MANUAL_ROLLS always runs one at a time.
REPLAY_BATTLES: Battle replays (2026-10-20, INTEGRATION__replay): battles 1..REPLAY_BATTLES of a run are each saved as a self-contained HTML page in REPLAY_DIR (relative = under the repo root) - a hex map to step through, both mechs' damage and heat, and the log of each step. 0 = none.
STATS: Battle statistics (2026-11-06, INTEGRATION__stats): every battle keeps an event log (each shot and physical attack, each unit's state at every turn's end, deaths) and the batch writes one HTML report from them (INTEGRATION__stats_report) into STATS_DIR (relative = under the repo root). It only reads the battle, so results are identical on or off; the reference-battle checks and the benchmark switch it off.
SAVE_STATE_TURNS: Saved states (2026-11-03, INTEGRATION__saved_state): at the end of the turns listed, battles 1..SAVE_STATE_BATTLES of a run each write a file to SAVE_STATE_DIR holding everything needed to play on from there - the units, the board as it stands, the dice and the bots' memories. Load one with `python INTEGRATION__saved_state.py <file>` to play the rest of the battle. SAVE_STATE_TURNS: () = none; (3, 5) = after turns 3 and 5; "all" = every turn.
SAVE_STATE_ROUND_TRIP: Test switch (tests/check_reference_logs.py --round-trip): after EVERY turn the battle is saved, reloaded from the saved text, and played on from the reloaded copy. The log must match a battle that never stopped, byte for byte.
USE_FASTCORE: Compiled hot loops (2026-11-03, trial): use the Rust module `fastcore` (built from fastcore/ with maturin) where it is installed. Speed only - the same answers as the Python; False (or not installed) = pure Python.
FASTCORE_PRICING: With fastcore: let the Rust fire table price a missile / special weapon itself when the planner can describe it in numbers (fire_modes.Planner.price_spec), instead of asking the planner row by row (2026-11-06; same answers - FIRE_TABLE_VERIFY checks). False = the Rust calls the planner back.
FASTCORE_MOVEMENT: With fastcore: the walking end states of a mover (ranged_combat._movement_options: the movement table, its states and their terrain PSRs) come from the Rust search (fastcore.PathBoard) on a board with terrain PSRs and no live hazards. 2026-11-06; same answers - tests/test_fastcore.py compares.
WEAPONS_CACHE_VERIFY: Test switch (tests/test_fire_tables.py): every damage_resolution.get_weapons answer that comes from its cache is compared with a fresh scan of the mech's slots (2026-11-06).
FASTCORE_LOS: With fastcore: the line of sight between two hexes (los_cache.pair_info's trace, Core pp.56-58) comes from the Rust copy (fastcore.LosBoard). 2026-11-06; same answers - tests/test_fastcore.py compares every pair.
FIRE_TABLE_VERIFY: Test switch (tests/test_fire_tables.py): every weapon choice a shared fire table answers in movement scoring is recomputed from scratch and must match (slow); the tables are also kept from turn to turn, so the key must catch every change of state.
TIMING: Where the time goes (2026-10-21, INTEGRATION__timing): TIMING prints a table of the time spent in each part of the turn after every batch (it only reads the clock - results don't change). PROFILE_FUNCTIONS = N also lists the N functions with the most time of their own (cProfile; about 2x slower). 0 = off.
PILOTING: Resting default only - see module docstring (2026-10-18). The real value per roll is each mech's own MECH_*_CONFIG["piloting"].
MECH_RED_CONFIG: DROPPED vs the old TEAM_RED/TEAM_BLUE shape (superseded, not carried forward): "weapons" list (real weapons now come from MECHSIM__equipment.get_weapons() on the parsed mech), "walking_mp"/ "running_mp"/"jumping_mp" (computed live from mech_state, not static), "max_hp"/"current_hp" (tracked on the BattleMech instance itself). "bot" (optional, 2026-10-27, INTEGRATION__bots): which bot decides for this unit - None = BOT below.
BOT: Which bot drives a unit when its MECH_*_CONFIG has no "bot" key (Daniel, 2026-10-27, INTEGRATION__bots): "gladiator" - this project's bot (movement_selection, weapon_selection, ...) "princess"  - a clone of MegaMek's Princess bot (v0.50.07: its path ranker, fire control and physical choice - INTEGRATION__princess, INTEGRATION__princess_fire; PROJECT_MAP Section 6, "Princess clone")
PRINCESS_VERSION: Princess's behavior sliders (MegaMek BehaviorSettings, each 0-10); 5 is MegaMek's "DEFAULT" behavior. Values: fall shame 10/40/80/100/160/500..500, bravery 0.1-3.0 in steps of 0.3, hyper-aggression 0.25/0.5/1/1.5/2/2.5/3/3.5/ 10/50/500, self-preservation 2.5-25 in steps of 2.5, then 30. Which Princess (2026-10-27, Daniel: "Clone the entire modern suit for Princess"): "modern"  - MegaMek main as of commit fd2edfb (2026-10-26): postures, the close- range pull, position holding, physical threat weights, movement-heat and TSM-aware fire control (INTEGRATION__princess_modern) "0.50.07" - the classic ranker first cloned (INTEGRATION__princess)
PRINCESS_GROUP: The group sliders (2026-10-28, INTEGRATION__princess_group; BehaviorSettings defaults): the friends' centre, per hex of distance (BasicPathRanker.calculateMutualSupportMod) The group behaviors on or off (2026-10-28, Daniel: Princess's mutual support, crowding, ...). Off gives the duel-only Princess the earlier recorded runs were made with (still weighing every enemy and the force's posture, but with no pull toward its friends or its own earlier ground).
LEGATE: Legate (2026-10-28, Daniel): the multi-unit layer that runs at the start of each Movement Phase so a Gladiator-driven unit is not blind to the other enemies (INTEGRATION__legate). False = every Gladiator plans against its nearest foe alone, as before. Duels are unchanged either way (one enemy). ON by default since 2026-10-29 (Daniel: "Legate on by default in multi unit games." - with the Gladiator target stub it took Gladiator from 0 to 4 wins in 20 12 v 12 battles, Change Record).
LEGATE_ITERATIONS: Legate's IF/THEN search: how many rounds (each round every enemy unit answers, then every unit of the asking side answers). A unit that picks a hex it already tried is locked at its best attempt.
LEGATE_FIRE_SPLIT: How much of an enemy's future fire a Gladiator expects to draw in its life-left estimate (INTEGRATION__legate.fire_share, 2026-10-29): "proportional" (its slice of what that enemy could deal across the team) or "none" (all of it - the first version, which made lights dive in alone).
LEGATE_SPLIT_THIS_TURN: alone it stalled battles (2026-10-29) The same share for THIS turn's damage (2026-10-30): without it the split makes HP worth more while this turn's damage still counts every enemy as shooting the mover (session 15 probe: 3.4 enemies counted, 0.63 really fired) - a mismatch. Only has an effect with LEGATE_FIRE_SPLIT "proportional".
LEGATE_COHESION: Herding (INTEGRATION__legate._Herd, 2026-10-29, Daniel's shape): a spot an enemy can reach costs LEGATE_HERD_WEIGHT damage for each hex it lies beyond the support of every teammate that can see one of those enemies (support: the end of the teammate's medium bracket, long if it stands still); no teammate sees one: LEGATE_HERD_UNSEEN_GAP hexes. Placeholder weights; off by default (A/B 2026-10-29). Cohesion (INTEGRATION__legate._Cohesion, 2026-10-30, Daniel: "Reward staying within a range braket of its allies, stronger at short, much weaker at long. And how many allies are in mutual support range."): for each teammate (where it will end), a spot inside its short / medium / long bracket (its best weapon for each) earns LEGATE_COHESION_REWARD[bracket], and one in mutual support range (within both units' support_range: medium, long when standing still) LEGATE_COHESION_MUTUAL more; damage points, taken off the damage the spot is expected to take; all times LEGATE_COHESION_SCALE. Placeholder weights.
LEGATE_COHESION_MAX_ALLIES: Refinements (2026-10-30, after the first cohesion A/B balled the force up): only the LEGATE_COHESION_MAX_ALLIES best-rewarding teammates count (None = all), and with LEGATE_COHESION_THREATENED_ONLY a spot no enemy (at its estimated spot) can reach needs no support and counts as fully supported.
LEGATE_COHESION_PAIRING: Whose brackets pair two units (2026-10-30, Daniel: "A fire support unit in the back will feel like its out of position because its not in cohesion with a short ranged back stabber up front. The back stabber however will feel fine since it has covering fire."): "ally" - the teammate's brackets (does it cover me) and mutual support inside BOTH support ranges (the shorter pulls everyone in); "either" - the better covering of the two (whichever unit covers the other) and support inside EITHER support range.
LEGATE_HERDING: 2 a hex changed half the battles but not the results (A/B 2026-10-29)
LEGATE_TEAM_VALUE: The team's future damage in a Gladiator's move score (INTEGRATION__legate._TeamFire, 2026-10-29, Daniel: "aware of the expected distribution of enemy fire ... how that distribution changed across its entire force, and the expected loss of future damage"): the enemy's fire this turn is distributed over the whole team with the mover at the spot being scored, and the score is dealt + the team's future damage - "sum" (each unit's life-left term, times its chance of living through the turn) or "product" (Daniel's SUM(future damage) x SUM(future vulnerability), over the team's size); None = off (the mover's own term).
LEGATE_TEAM_FIRE_MODEL: whom each enemy shoots: its most-hurt target not already doomed
LEGATE_TEAM_EXCHANGE: The exchange (2026-10-29, Daniel: "a valid tactic is to saturate them with targets while swarming them down ... 'some of us may die, but that's a sacrifice I'm willing to make'"): with a team value, also count the enemy's future damage our team's fire takes off the board this turn (our fire distributed by the same rule, each enemy's kill curve), times LEGATE_TEAM_EXCHANGE_WEIGHT - so a move is worth our team's future damage plus the enemy's we remove.
DEPLOYMENT: Deployment (2026-10-19, Core p.37): "home_edge"   - deployment roll; the loser picks a home edge, the winner gets the opposite one; mechs enter along it on turn 1 "fixed_hexes" - start at MECH_*_CONFIG hex/facing (a set scenario)
HOME_EDGE_CHOICE: Which edge the deployment-roll loser picks: "random", or "N"/"E"/"S"/"W".
DEPLOYMENT_PLACED: Placed or walking on (Daniel, 2026-11-19: "that formation logic is supposed to be standard kit"). True (the default): before turn 1 each unit is PLACED in a hex of its home-edge row (up to DEPLOYMENT_DEPTH in), standing where its bot would put it (Princess and CASPAR: MegaMek's deployment logic; Gladiator and Hydra: the shared placement), as MegaMek deploys. False: the rule book's walk-on (Core p.37): each 'Mech moves onto the board from its home edge when its turn to move comes, its movement counted from the first full hex. A unit with no free hex on the edge still walks on. Rust engine only.
DEPLOYMENT_DEPTH: How far in from its home edge a mech may start its movement (Daniel, 2026-10-21: "Its value is the number of hexes in from the edge that a mech can start its movement"): 0 = the edge hexes only (Core p.37). Read here as hexes 0..N in, so 3 = the edge row and the three rows behind it.
DEPLOYMENT_STUCK_DEPTH: Daniel's "I can't enter / stuck terrain" override: when no hex within DEPLOYMENT_DEPTH lets this mech enter AND still reach the far side of the map (by walking or jumping - "stuck" is no path to the other side for this unit), it may start this many hexes in instead. INTEGRATION__deployment.
MECH_RED_MTF: .mtf files for a headless run (2026-10-18). None = open the tkinter picker. Default matchup (Daniel, 2026-10-20): the Kontio vs the Hammerhead, the example battle in the game's starter set ("Asymptote is an uninteresting match"). The Asymptote II tripod stays in data/ for the tests.
FORCES: "hex", "facing"  where it starts, with DEPLOYMENT = "fixed_hexes" only Example, a lance against a lance: FORCES = [{"team": "Red", "mtf": "Atlas AS7-D.mtf", "count": 4}, {"team": "Blue", "mtf": "Hammerhead.mtf", "count": 4}]
FOE_CHOICE: Whom each bot plans its movement against (its "foe"; the other enemies are not modeled by the movement scoring - independent bots) and fires at. "nearest": the nearest enemy (a fire target must also be in sight). Section 6, 'Target choice'.
DOMINO_DODGE: A 'Mech that passes its domino-effect PSR may step one hex forward or back out of the way instead of being pushed on (Core p.114). MegaMek's bots never do ("TODO: Bots should figure out how to step out", BotClient) - so neither does this one. True: it steps aside whenever a legal hex is open (forward first).
ESCALATING_CYCLE_ON_ODD_TURNS: Radical heat sinks, MASC, supercharger: Escalating Failure systems, used on a 1-turn-on / 1-turn-off cycle (Daniel). True = "on" turns are the odd turns (1, 3, 5...); False = even turns. (Since 2026-10-20 whether to use them is a stub - STUB_ESCALATING_USE below; "cycle" follows this setting.)
TSM_MIN_HEAT: Triple-strength myomer is driven by min_heat (Daniel): a TSM mech's min_heat is raised to at least this (TSM works at 9+ heat), and its max_heat to at least its min_heat.
AMS_HEAT_LIMIT: Anti-Missile Systems (Core p.206, INTEGRATION__ams): an AMS engages the incoming missile hits it can, unless that would leave the mech's projected end-of-turn heat above max(its max_heat, AMS_HEAT_LIMIT). 13 = the last heat level with no shutdown roll (p.104). Matters mostly for laser AMS (7 heat IS / 5 Clan per engagement; a standard AMS makes 1).
TARGET_HEAT_WORTH: Worth of one point of heat put on the enemy (flamers, plasma - pp.102, 189), counted as this much damage when the bot prices a heat-causing weapon. PLACEHOLDER (Claude 2026-10-20) until Daniel sets it - without it a plasma cannon (no damage, 2D6 heat) would never be worth firing.
TASER_EFFECT_WORTH: A BattleMech Taser hit's effect on the target (TO:AUE p.158: shut down 3 turns on 11+, else +2 to its Piloting / Gunnery and 5 heat a turn for 3 turns), counted as this much damage when the bot prices a Taser shot. PLACEHOLDER (Claude 2026-10-27) until Daniel sets it - without it a Taser (1 damage for 6 heat) would never be worth firing.
TSEMP_EFFECT_WORTH: A TSEMP hit's effect (Interstellar Operations pp.90-91: interference or a shutdown through the next turn), counted as this much damage when the bot prices a TSEMP shot - and IMP missile effects (+1 to hit, -1 MP, hostile ECM through the next turn), this much per +1 level. PLACEHOLDERS (Claude 2026-10-28) until Daniel sets them, in the research pile with TASER_EFFECT_WORTH and the worth of cluster weapons - without them a TSEMP (no damage) would never be worth firing.
AIMED_SHOT_LOCATION: Aimed shots at immobile targets (shut down / crew unconscious, Core p.70): the location every eligible weapon aims at, or None for no aimed shots. "Head" uses +3 instead of the -4 immobile modifier.
PROMPT_FOR_MAP: Ported from PATHFINDER__config.py. orchestrator._load_map() loads DEFAULT_BOARD_PATH (one board), or - with STITCH_MAPS - the boards named in STITCH_BOARDS laid out row-major in a STITCH_GRID_COLS x STITCH_GRID_ROWS grid (board_parser.stitch_boards; 2026-10-28, for company-size fights). PROMPT_FOR_MAP = True asks a person for the map at the start of a run (INTEGRATION__map_picker: one board or a stitched grid, from data/ and the data/maps.zip pack; Enter repeats last time's pick) and writes the answer into the settings below. Headless runs keep the configured map.
STITCH_BOARDS: Board files (under DATA_DIR), row-major: left to right, then down. Same-row boards must share a height and same-column boards a width. Seams follow MegaMek (Daniel, 2026-11-06): boards abut; only after an odd-width board is one blank column inserted, to keep the column parity. Use one name several times for a repeated board. Example, a 2 x 1 field (32 x 17) of two 16x17 maps: STITCH_MAPS = True; STITCH_GRID_COLS, STITCH_GRID_ROWS = 2, 1 STITCH_BOARDS = ["16x17_Grassland_1.board", "16x17_Scattered_Woods.board"]
STUB_UNKNOWN_DAMAGE_TYPE: (STUB_MOVEMENT_POLICY / STUB_NO_LOS_FALLBACK removed 2026-10-19: movement selection is real - INTEGRATION__movement_selection; knobs are in the MOVEMENT SETTINGS block below.) (STUB_WALK_PSR_AS removed 2026-10-19: walking never forces a PSR - Core p.111.) (STUB_POST_STANDUP removed 2026-10-19: a mech that stands moves on with its remaining MP, any facing - Core p.51, orchestrator._phase_movement.) (STUB_HIT_TABLE_SIDE removed 2026-10-19: attack direction now comes from geometry - INTEGRATION__attack_resolution.attack_side, Core p.73.) (STUB_CLUSTER_GROUPING removed 2026-10-19: cluster damage groupings come from the Core rules - INTEGRATION__weapon_rules, SRM 2 / LRM, MRM 5 / ATM 6.) Damage type used when equipment.json has damage_type null (only matters for special armor types in armor_rules): "BALLISTIC" / "ENERGY" / "MISSILE"
STUB_MUNITION_POLICY: --- Bot decisions still being researched (Daniel, 2026-10-20: "How a bot determines what rate to fire at, If it should use MASC, or what kind of ammo to use (Apollo goes in this catagory) is still a matter of research"). The options are real rules (INTEGRATION__fire_modes, INTEGRATION__electronics, INTEGRATION__equipment_systems); these stubs pick one. --- Which ammunition kind / guidance / Apollo mode a weapon fires (LB-X slug or cluster, ATM standard / ER / HE, MML LRM / SRM, Artemis / Narc-equipped or standard missiles, Narc homing or explosive pods): "greedy"   - most expected damage this shot (a homing pod: its worth); ties keep standard ammunition "standard" - standard ammunition / slugs whenever there is some "random"   - a seeded random pick
STUB_RATE_OF_FIRE: How many shots an Ultra (1-2) / Rotary (1-6) autocannon fires: "max" - as many as it can (ammo permitting); "single" - one; "greedy" - most expected damage this shot (a Rotary's jam risk isn't priced)
STUB_UNJAM: Try to unjam a jammed Rotary AC (that turn: stand still or walk only). True = whenever it's jammed and the mech isn't prone.
STUB_ESCALATING_USE: When MASC / a supercharger / a radical heat sink system is used: "cycle"  - Daniel's 1-turn-on / 1-turn-off default (ESCALATING_CYCLE_ON_ODD_TURNS) "always" / "never"
STUB_CHARGE_SPIKES: Equipment choices (Daniel, 2026-10-21: wired, the decisions deferred - each is a stub in INTEGRATION__stubs). Charge with torso spikes declared (p.196): True = always when the mech has them.
STUB_VIBROBLADE: Activate a vibroblade for its attack (p.196): "on" (fixed damage, heat) / "off".
STUB_RAISE_SHIELD: Raise a shield at the start of an attack phase (p.195): "never" / "always".
STUB_CONSOLE_SWAP: Command console End Phase seat swap (p.203): "when_needed" (pilot out or more hurt) / "never".
STUB_BLUE_SHIELD: Blue Shield particle field damper switched on (p.207): "on" / "off".
STUB_FIRE_TAG: TAG (p.200): designate the enemy before the Ranged Attack Phase? "when_useful" (the 'Mech has homing artillery rounds to use it) / "always" / "never".
STUB_TAG_AIM: TAG aim: "mech" (the enemy - homing rounds hit it in full) / "hex" (the ground it stands on - an easier shot, homing rounds then do 5 AE to it) / "easier" (the lower target number).
STUB_SPOT: Spotting for indirect fire (Core p.70; Rust engine only, session 30): does a unit spot this turn? "never" (the default: the bots' own spotting logic is built elsewhere; a TAG hit still spots) / "when_useful" (the enemy it sees that the most friends can't see but could hit indirectly; it keeps firing, +1 to its own attacks).
STUB_DISTANT_ARTILLERY: Distant artillery (Arrow IV / Thumper / Sniper at 18+ hexes, landing next turn; Core p.182; Rust engine only): offer the shot? "never" (the default: the bots' own artillery targeting is built elsewhere) / "at_target" (at the target's hex now, valued as if it stays there - a crude placeholder).
STUB_SPLIT_FIRE: Split fire (several targets in a turn; Core p.64; Rust engine only): "never" (the default: Princess / CASPAR fire an ordinary 'Mech at one target as MegaMek does; Gladiator / Hydra don't split fire yet) / "spare_weapons" (every other enemy in sight, nearest first, with the weapons not yet used - a crude placeholder).
STUB_CAPACITOR_START: PPC capacitors (p.188): start the battle charged? "empty" / "charged".
STUB_CAPACITOR_CHARGE: Charge a PPC capacitor instead of firing its PPC? "never" / "when_idle" (whenever the PPC isn't fired).
STUB_GLADIATOR_TARGET: Whom a GLADIATOR unit shoots when two or more enemies are on the board (2026-10-29, Daniel: "a good test to stub in until we teach gladiator how to focus fire and account for target saturation"): "princess_plan" - Princess's target choice: each enemy scored by Princess's firing-plan utility, with the damage the unit's teammates already declared this phase counted (an enemy they are expected to kill scores low - focus fire without overkill). Gladiator still picks its own weapons at the target, and its declared damage is counted for the teammates who fire after it. "nearest"       - the old pick (forces.choose_target: in sight, a weapon bears, nearest). "kill_curve"    - NOT a stub: Gladiator's own fire director (2026-10-29, Daniel: "splitting fire to wreck 2 units is better then hard killing 1 and grazing the other"). Each enemy is scored by how much this unit's expected damage raises the enemy's chance of a mission kill (INTEGRATION__kill_curve), on top of what teammates already declared at it, times the enemy's worth (KILL_CURVE_WEIGHT). Its declaration is counted too. Duels are unchanged either way (one enemy).
STUB_MISSION_KILL: A mission kill for the kill curve (INTEGRATION__kill_curve; 2026-10-29, Daniel: "an immobile, weaponless torso with a leg on the ground is still dangerous, if it can spot ... the weight for spotting has not been evaluated yet"). An immobile 'Mech is already destroyed under the default rules (FIGHT_TO_THE_DEATH off). "destroyed"         - destroyed only: a 'Mech with no gun that can still move, kick or spot fights on. "no_ranged_weapons" - also once no ranged weapon is left that can fire (spotting worth nothing).
KILL_CURVE_GROUP: The kill curve (INTEGRATION__kill_curve, 2026-10-29): the chance a 'Mech is mission-killed by N more points of damage from its current state, from a small Monte Carlo on the engine's damage code.
KILL_CURVE_TRIALS: trials a curve (one side of one 'Mech in one damage state; cached)
KILL_CURVE_MAX_DAMAGE: a trial stops here (more than a turn's fire on one 'Mech)
KILL_CURVE_WEIGHT: What counts as a mission kill ("no longer able to support its teams combat operations", Daniel 2026-10-29) is a STUB while spotting has no worth: see STUB_MISSION_KILL below. An enemy's worth in the fire director: "output" (its damage a turn, INTEGRATION__future_damage - Daniel: "Expected damage output from the target / its vulnerability") or "none" (every kill alike).
KILL_CURVE_PROGRESS_WEIGHT: Softening in the fire director (2026-10-29): what a share of a kill paid toward later turns is worth beside kill chance added this turn (mine / the damage the enemy still needs). 1 = a full kill's worth of softening counts as a kill now; near 0, only kills this turn count (a long shot that adds 1% on a hurt enemy then beats a full volley into a fresh one).
MOVE_ORDER: Gladiator's firing order within its side's selections (2026-10-29, Daniel: "Big guns first followed by smaller guns. Its the same rule used on a mech, just applied to the entire formation."): "big_guns_first" (most expected damage at any enemy now declares first) or "roster" (list order). Which of a side's units takes its Movement Phase selection next (Daniel, 2026-11-07: "how much does order matter at all"). "index" (default): Princess's move index, the higher first (forces.move_index). "random": a deterministic shuffle (seeded from the units' names and hexes, so it never touches the battle's dice). "reverse": the LOWEST index first. A test switch, for baseline_battery.py --move-order. "tiered" (Daniel's design, 2026-11-07, INTEGRATION__tiers): for Gladiator units - stand-still units first (farthest first), then units whose movement footprint is outside the enemy's, then units that may be flanked, then units that cannot escape (slower first inside a tier); tiers 2 and 3 plan their two-ply against the highest-threat enemy that could flank them; applies when entering the battlefield too.
PERIL: PERIL (2026-11-07, Daniel's peril heat map; INTEGRATION__peril): how Legate prices the damage a spot takes from the enemies OTHER than the mover's foe. "off" (default): each at the one spot Legate estimates it ends in (or its real spot once it has moved). "peak" / "mean": from the whole of where it COULD end (its movement footprint, line of sight and cover applied) - the most any one spot would deal there, or the average over its spots. PERIL_BLEND = the share the field takes, the point estimate the rest (1.0 = the field only). Placeholder weights; only with Legate on.
STACK: STACK (2026-11-07, Daniel: stack the team's damage maps on a target's movement profile up to what kills it; INTEGRATION__stack): a candidate spot earns STACK_WEIGHT x the coverage it adds - the team's summed damage over each enemy's footprint, capped at that enemy's HP, averaged (STACK_QUANTILE None) or read at a low quantile - on top of the damage it deals. Only with Legate on. Placeholder weight; off by default.
TRIAGE: TRIAGE (2026-11-07, Daniel: peril / toughness tiers; INTEGRATION__triage): each unit's peril (the damage the enemy side could bring to its hex) / its toughness, ranked over the team. The TRIAGE_FRACTION highest are HOT: the damage a spot would take counts TRIAGE_HOT_RECEIVED times. The same share at the bottom are COOL: the damage a spot would deal counts TRIAGE_COOL_DEALT times. Only with Legate on and three or more units. Placeholder weights; off by default.
MOVEMENT_TWO_PLY: INTEGRATION__movement_selection (Daniel, 2026-10-19). Not BattleTech rules: the scoring and search policy for where a mech ends its movement. score = dealt / (received + PSR cost + MOVEMENT_RATIO_EPSILON) The first mover scores each spot by the second mover's modeled reply (two-ply).
MOVEMENT_SEARCH: Movement search (2026-10-21, Daniel's "guess and follow"; the default since 2026-10-21 - Daniel: "I think it should become the default"): "grid"       - a 1-in-7 net of the reachable hexes (the hex grid's own spacing: every hex is a net hex or touches exactly one; the mover's own hex is always in it), then from the best MOVEMENT_SEARCH_STARTS net hexes follow uphill: look at the unchecked neighbours of the best hex so far, move to the best of them while it improves. A hex "looked at" scores all its facings and modes. No dice involved. A second mover (knowing where its enemy stands) also always looks at the 6 hexes around the enemy (melee). "exhaustive" - every reachable spot ("perfect"; the original). "if_then"    - (Daniel's IF/THEN, 2026-10-28; MOVEMENT_SEARCH only): the first mover asks "If I hold still then" where would the second mover reply, takes its best spot against that reply, asks where the reply to that would be, and so on, back and forth; it stops when an attempt scores no better (two-ply score) than the one before and keeps that one before, or picks a spot twice. A second mover scores every spot, as "exhaustive". "short_list" - (Daniel's "simple short list", 2026-10-24): the first mover looks for the reply only on a rule-of- thumb list of hexes - next to the first mover, the replier's own hex, and the hexes at the MOVEMENT_SHORT_LIST_DROPS ranges where the replier's damage drops most, or one past where the first mover's does. Each hex is scored once per movement mode at its best TMM, facing the first mover (its facing isn't searched). An immobile or prone replier keeps the full model. As MOVEMENT_SEARCH ("Short-Short", 2026-10-27: "both sides are only picking from their own short lists"): the mover's own hex and the hexes at those ranges from the enemy, best few states per hex (movement_selection.own_short_list), each with the look-ahead when moving first. MOVEMENT_SEARCH: how a mech picks its OWN spot (first mover: which spots get the two-ply look-ahead; second mover: its real pick). MOVEMENT_ASSUMED_ENEMY_SEARCH: how a first mover ASSUMES the second mover picks its reply in the look-ahead. Per side (Daniel, 2026-10-21: "See how much of an advantage perfect knowledge is vs close enough"): MECH_RED_CONFIG / MECH_BLUE_CONFIG may set "search" and "assumes_enemy_search" to override these two for that mech.
MOVEMENT_ASSUMED_ENEMY_SEARCH: "short_list" is the default since 2026-10-24 (Daniel: "we push 'Simple Short list' for the first movers evaluation"); "grid" was the default before that.
MOVEMENT_SEARCH_STARTS: "grid": how many of the best net hexes to follow uphill from
MOVEMENT_IF_THEN_STEPS: "if_then": 0 = the climb (stop when an attempt scores no better, keep the one before); N > 0 = up to N attempts whatever they score, stopping early on a hex it already tried, then the best-scoring attempt (Daniel, 2026-10-28: "run like 10 to 15 steps").
MOVEMENT_IF_THEN_NEIGHBOUR_CLIMB: "if_then": True = after the back and forth, climb from the best attempt's hex to better neighbouring hexes by the two-ply score (Daniel, 2026-10-28: "I like option 2"). IF/THEN isn't meant as a single 'Mech's default search (Daniel, 2026-10-28): in multi-unit games it gives the threat vector of farther units, while stronger searches handle the immediate threats.
MOVEMENT_SHORT_LIST_DROPS: "short_list": how many damage-drop ranges per mech go on the list, and the pre-to-hit number the rough damage-by-range curve is read at (gunnery 4 + about 2 for movement).
MOVEMENT_SHORT_LIST_GRID: Short-Short (own search "short_list", 2026-10-27): True = Daniel's grid search ("guess and follow") over the short-list hexes instead of scoring them all (Daniel: "if short list hexes tend to be continuous ... a grid search prune on them would reduce the total that need to be checked").
MOVEMENT_GRID_SPIN: "grid": which of the two mirror-image 1-in-7 nets (2026-10-21, Daniel's spin A/B). The range-3 net hexes are "2 hexes out, then 1 turning clockwise" or "... counter-clockwise".
MOVEMENT_RATIO_EPSILON: added to the denominator so no-return-fire spots don't divide by zero
MOVEMENT_EXPOSURE_WEIGHTING: Armor-exposure weighting: damage that lands on thin armor counts for more, in both directions (what this mech deals and what it receives). A shot from the front counts 1.0; other sides are scaled by how much more of a location's durability a point of damage uses there, clamped to [MIN, MAX]. See the movement_selection docstring.
MOVEMENT_PSR_COST: Add the expected fall damage of the Movement Phase PSR a Run/Jump would force (only a damaged mech has one) to the damage received.
MOVEMENT_STRUCTURE_WEIGHT: Internal-structure damage counts for more than armor damage (Daniel, 2026-10-19): per weapon, the part of a hit that gets past a location's armor and into its structure counts this many times. 1.0 = off. See INTEGRATION__structure_weight.
MOVEMENT_OBJECTIVE: Which movement objective scores a spot (Daniel, 2026-10-20 - an option to test): "ratio"    - dealt / (received + PSR cost + MOVEMENT_RATIO_EPSILON) (Daniel, 2026-10-19) "lifetime" - dealt + (my HP left after this turn / the enemy's future damage per turn) x my future damage per turn: the damage this mech can expect to deal before it is destroyed. Fights when this turn's trade beats the trades it can expect later; a spot that gets it destroyed (or pushed off the board) keeps only its dealt. Future damage: INTEGRATION__future_damage. HP is armor + rear armor + MOVEMENT_STRUCTURE_WEIGHT x structure (the same units as dealt / received).
MOVEMENT_LIFETIME_INITIATIVE: odds of winning initiative (scales both sides; cancels out)
MOVEMENT_LIFETIME_ATTACKER_MODE: the attacker's assumed movement for future damage (AMM, heat)
MOVEMENT_LIFETIME_FUTURE_FLOOR: future damage per turn is never taken below this (no divide by zero)
MOVEMENT_LIFETIME_HISTORY_K: History blend (Daniel, 2026-10-21: "We can't predict the future. But we can record the past ... a mech that is doing well will continue to do well, but a mech that is losing becomes more desperate to inflict damage"). Each future damage per turn becomes (K x the estimate + damage actually done so far) / (K + turns fought) where damage done = how much the OTHER mech's HP (same units: armor + k x structure) has really gone down, and turns fought count from the first turn either mech lost HP. K = how many turns' worth of trust the estimate gets: on the first turn it is all estimate, later the record takes over. None = off.
CHARGES: Charge attacks (Core p.78, INTEGRATION__charge, 2026-10-20): the mover may charge an enemy that has finished moving, when a charge in that movement mode beats the best ordinary attack and its score beats the normal pick.
DFA: Death from above (Core pp.79-80, INTEGRATION__dfa, 2026-10-20): same decision.
CLUB_PICKUP: Picking up clubs (Core p.79, INTEGRATION__clubs). ON since 2026-10-21 (Daniel: "Clubs do not block weapons fire ... May as well have mechs pick them up if they have nothing better to do"): a mech that fires nothing in a Ranged phase picks up a club in its hex. Was off (2026-10-20). A smarter decision waits for the bot's future-capability planning (PROJECT_MAP Section 6, "Memo").
POOL_CLUSTER_DAMAGE: Cluster damage pooling (Daniel, 2026-10-20: "all cluster damage of a specific size is added up and then applied. So 2 LRM 20's that both rolled for 12 damage would do 5,5,5,5,4"). True: in a Ranged phase, every Cluster hit's damage from one attacker with the same grouping size (and damage type) is summed, then split into groupings. False: each attack's hits are grouped on their own (Core pp.74, 87 read per attack). Default False since 2026-10-21 (Daniel: "Follow the rules, not my calls") - the rules as written.
FLOATING_CRITICALS: Floating Criticals (Core p.95, optional): a Hit Location roll of 2 re-rolls where the shot lands and the critical-hit chance goes there. False = the standard Through-Armor Critical (p.91): the damage stays on the torso the 2 hit, plus one extra critical-hit check there.
FIGHT_TO_THE_DEATH: Fight to the death (Daniel, 2026-10-20). False (default, Daniel's rule - kept 2026-10-21: "fight to the death is set to off because it saves time when the situation is hopeless"): the fight is over when a mech is rendered immobile for good - a destroyed gyro or both legs destroyed counts as destroyed. True (the rules as written): a destroyed gyro means a fall and no standing up (p.98) but the mech fights on from the ground; both legs destroyed makes it immobile (pp.49, 90) and it fights on propped up (p.67); a mech is destroyed when immobile with no ranged weapons left (p.99). (Crippled / forced withdrawal: a later option.)
PASSIVE_BUILDINGS: Passive buildings (Daniel, 2026-10-21: "treat buildings as passive terrain. Blocks LOS. Can't be entered. Can be jumped onto"). True: a building hex is a block as tall as its roof - it blocks LOS like a hill (p.135), ground movement can't enter it, a 'Mech can jump onto the roof (p.50) and walk roof to roof (same level or one lower) but not off a roof (p.134); nothing damages it. False: the full building rules (forced entry, moving inside, damage, collapse - Core pp.130-136) - not built yet, so a map with buildings refuses to load.
NARC_HOMING_FOR_FORCE: Narc homing ammo for the force (Daniel, 2026-11-20; Rust engine only, the Python ignores it): "if a team has Narc or iNarc with homing beacon ammo on its side, all standard LRM and SRM ammo in their force is replaced with Narc homing ammo." True: when the battle starts, every standard LRM / SRM bin of such a team fires Narc-capable missiles (Core pp.188, 193). False: rules as written, each bin as the unit file says. A scenario without the setting plays False. False HERE on purpose: every setting of this file goes into the Python's fixtures, and the frozen Python never applies the rule; the Rust engine's own default (engine/defaults/config.json, the Combat Lab and btsim) is True.
RENDER_TURN_STATIC: Ported from PATHFINDER__config.py / MECHSIM__config.py. Not called from anywhere yet - useful for a single debug game, not a real Monte Carlo batch.
CLUSTER_HITS_TABLE_COLUMNS: COMPLEXITY FLAG: roll_2d6()'s bulk-numpy-cache + MANUAL_ROLLS + set_active_rng fallback chain has real reasoning behind it (perf history, seeding gotchas) - trimmed to essentials here per the 2-sentence rule; flagging that the full history lives in MECHSIM__config.py's old HELP tags if it's ever needed.
